proposals.title: Test whether eligible graph identities improve perturbation prediction
proposals.claim: On independent-embryo perturbation validation, an eligible biological prior will exceed degree-preserving randomized priors by a prespecified practical margin in de_direction. This is an untested hypothesis, not a causal-edge claim.
proposals.mechanism: Biological edge identities may transfer response information to measured targets, raising de_direction and de_score; mmd_u and severity_slope guard against a benefit driven by wrong composition or magnitude. Match architecture, graph degree, tuning budget and training-only preprocessing.
proposals.falsifier: After data acquisition, run true/no/coexpression graphs and repeated degree-preserving randomized priors on identical embryo splits. Kill the claim if the true-minus-random de_direction interval fails to exceed the preregistered practical margin.

evidence.says: Requests no, known, learned and randomized prior controls; warns random-prior gains may be regularization.

evidence.ref: Roohani et al., GEARS, Nature Biotechnology, online 2023 / volume 2024, doi:10.1038/s41587-023-01905-6; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-023-01905-6
evidence.says: Uses coexpression and GO graphs with large perturbation screens; discussion requires matching cell type or condition for reliable prediction.

evidence.ref: Pratapa et al., BEELINE, Nature Methods 2020, doi:10.1038/s41592-019-0690-6; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-019-0690-6
evidence.says: Reports moderate precision in benchmarked GRN inference; does not validate this project's edges.

peer_responses.on: causal-r1-1: WT plus Mab21l2 does not identify Gata4 responses
peer_responses.because: Endorse nonidentifiability; eligible priors can still predict. Randomized controls test graph identities, not direction or direct regulation. GEARS uses coexpression/GO. Gata4 measured-paper exposure needs separate stage/allele provenance before predictive use.

declined: Decline attention-as-causality and scaling Mab21l2 deltas into held-out knockouts. One perturbation does not identify unrelated interventions; absent data prevent testing panel coverage or historical gene rankings.
